EXPLANATION: The intense 1005 cm⁻¹ band is a classic benzene ring-breathing mode that is especially strong for para-disubstituted rings; candidate 1 has a para-chloro-phenyl substituent. The pair of bands at 809 and 855 cm⁻¹ are consistent with para out-of-plane C–H deformation. The 750 cm⁻¹ band fits an aryl C–Cl stretch, supporting the presence of chlorine. Aliphatic and aromatic C–H stretches (2939–3064 cm⁻¹) and multiple ring modes (1588–1606 cm⁻¹) align with an aromatic alkyl compound. The lack of clear NH/OH stretches disfavors candidates containing NH/OH groups, whereas candidate 1 contains no such X–H. The peroxide functionality can also account for features in the 550–600 and ~850 cm⁻¹ regions.
